claim_text: On September 20, 2022, DOJ announced federal criminal charges against 47 defendants in six indictments and three criminal informations for alleged roles in a fraud scheme exploiting USDA child-nutrition reimbursements administered in Minnesota by MDE and sponsored in large part by Feeding Our Future.

amounts.notes: $250 million charging headline, not a restitution total; not proven_loss
more than $240 million fraudulently obtained and disbursed (then alleged)
more than $18 million administrative fees to FOF

review_notes: Actor class A. Do not treat $250 million as proven_loss. Indictment is merely an allegation (S01).

claim_text: On March 13, 2023, USAO-MN announced charges against 10 additional defendants across four indictments and two informations.

amounts.notes: Hussein and Lul Ali >$5 million received

review_notes: Actor class A. Journalism said this brought the total to 60; S02 itself does not state 60.

claim_text: On November 20, 2025, U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Ousman Camara was indicted in a nine-count indictment and is the 77th defendant indicted in the scheme.

claim_text: On November 24, 2025, U.S. District Judge Nancy E. Brasel sentenced Abdimajid Mohamed Nur to 120 months plus 3 years supervised release and ordered restitution of $47,920,514 for his role in the Empire Cuisine Feeding Our Future fraud (theft exceeding $47 million through the group's sites, as characterized by the USAO after trial).

amounts.notes: more than $47 million as demonstrated at trial — group/site loss

review_notes: Same restitution dollar figure appears for Abdiaziz Shafii Farah (S07/S21). Likely joint-and-several. Do not treat as two independent $47.9 million recoveries.

claim_text: Abdiaziz Farah pleaded guilty June 17, 2025, before Judge David S. Doty to one count of bribery of a juror (18 U.S.C. § 201). Five defendants were charged in the juror-bribery case (Abdiaziz Farah, Abdimajid Nur, Said Farah, Abdulkarim Farah, Ladan Ali); $120,000 cash was delivered to Juror 52 on 2024-06-02 and $200,000 cash was gathered.

amounts.notes: $120,000 cash delivered — bribe, not program loss
Nur plea agreed forfeiture of $120,000 + seized cash

claim_text: Abdulkarim Shafii Farah, 25, was sentenced by Judge Eric C. Tostrud to 57 months plus 1 year supervised release for his role in the juror-bribe plot.
review_notes: Not the July 2026 120-month sentence. Different person (Abdulkarim, not Abdiaziz) and different term (57 months, not 120).

claim_text: Journalism reports that Abdiaziz Shafii Farah was sentenced July 22, 2026, by Judge Eric C. Tostrud to 120 months for bribing a Feeding Our Future juror, consecutive to his 28-year fraud sentence.
review_notes: A DOJ OPA/IRS-CI page for that 120-month sentence was not retrieved. Do not upgrade Abdiaziz Farah's bribery status from pleaded to sentenced on this lead.

claim_text: After a 21-day jury trial (Feb 3-Mar 18, 2025), Aimee Marie Bock was convicted of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, four counts of wire fraud, conspiracy to commit federal programs bribery, and federal programs bribery. On May 22, 2026, she was sentenced to 500 months. Salim Ahmed Said was convicted on all counts tried, including section 666 bribery and section 1957 money laundering. Post-trial motions were denied August 22, 2025.

amounts.notes: >$240 million fraudulently obtained and disbursed — DOJ post-trial characterization, not a published restitution figure in S12
$310,000 daycare-center check treated by jury as bribe (S22)

supporting_passages.quote: This was a fraud vortex and you were at the epicenter of it.

claim_text: After a seven-week trial starting April 22, 2024, a jury convicted Abdiaziz Shafii Farah of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to commit federal programs bribery, false statements in a passport application, conspiracy to commit money laundering, two counts of federal programs bribery, six counts of wire fraud, and 11 counts of money laundering. On August 6, 2025, Judge Brasel sentenced him to 28 years plus 3 years SR. IRS-CI states restitution of $47,920,514 / $47.92 million.

amounts.notes: IRS-CI; full S07 page returned a historical stub on fetch
more than $47 million / 18 million meals claimed — USAO post-trial characterization of the Empire group

review_notes: Exact judgment PDF not downloaded. Same $47,920,514 as Nur — likely joint-and-several; do not sum.

claim_text: Charging and adjudicative documents in this corpus use: 18 U.S.C. section 1343 (wire fraud); 18 U.S.C. section 371 (conspiracy); 18 U.S.C. section 666 (federal programs bribery); 18 U.S.C. section 1956(a) (concealment money-laundering conspiracy); 18 U.S.C. section 1957; 18 U.S.C. section 201 (bribery of a juror). DOJ press releases also describe false statements in a passport application (Abdiaziz Farah).
review_notes: 18 U.S.C. section 1349 was not located in fetched charging text. Snyder v. United States, 603 U.S. 1 (2024) required the Bock court to treat section 666 as bribes not gratuities (S22).

claim_text: In a September 23, 2022, Minnesota Judicial Branch statement, the court stated that Judge John Guthmann never ordered MDE to resume payments to Feeding Our Future in April 2021 or at any other time, and that MDE voluntarily resumed payments.

supporting_passages.quote: Judge Guthmann never ordered the Department of Education to resume payments to FOF in April 2021, or at any other time.
Thereafter, the Department of Education voluntarily resumed making payments to FOF. The Department of Education was not ordered by the court to do so.
All of the MN Department of Education food reimbursement payments to FOF were made voluntarily, without any court order.

review_notes: Guthmann contradiction vs. judge-ordered-payments. The statement calls the Star Tribune line, the commissioner's April 4, 2022 Senate testimony, and Governor Walz's September 22, 2022 media comments false.

claim_text: Federal prosecutions collected here charge private site operators, vendors, FOF employees, and the FOF founder — actor class A. OLA findings concern MDE's failure to oversee (B) and being ill-prepared / using untrained investigators / asking FOF to investigate itself (C). No charging document in this corpus alleges that MDE officials knowingly committed the theft (D).
review_notes: Class D not supported for MDE officials in collected sources. Class E not supported.

claim_text: The September 13, 2022 indictment in United States v. Bock, 0:22-cr-00223, ECF 1, charges 14 caption defendants in 61 counts: Count 1 conspiracy to commit wire fraud under 18 U.S.C. §§ 371 and 1343 (Abdirahman Mohamud Ahmed not named in this count); Counts 2–14 wire fraud under § 1343; Count 15 conspiracy to commit federal-programs bribery under § 371; Counts 16–40 federal-programs bribery under §§ 666(a)(1)(B) and (a)(2), including a $310,000 Cosmopolitan-to-Bock check as Count 40; Count 41 money-laundering conspiracy under § 1956(h) (Bock not named; Abdirahman is); Counts 42–61 monetary transactions under § 1957. Caption statutes are 18 U.S.C. §§ 371, 666, 1343, 1956, and 1957. 18 U.S.C. § 1349 does not appear in this instrument.
